content.text: Add rate limiting to our API so a single client can't hammer the /search endpoint. Use a token bucket, configurable per-route.
Let me first look at how config is currently structured so the rate-limit settings fit the existing pattern.
Config is a simple class with class attributes. I'll add RATE_LIMIT_DEFAULT and a per-route override dict here so ops can tune limits without touching code.
Now I need the actual token bucket implementation. There's no existing middleware directory, so I'll create middleware.py with a RateLimiter class that reads config.py's RATE_LIMIT_OVERRIDES.
middleware.py needs to actually be wired into the request pipeline, so I'll edit routes.py to call RateLimiter.allow() before the /search handler runs, returning 429 if it fails.

routes.py references a shared rate_limiter instance that doesn't exist yet. I'll instantiate it in app_init.py alongside the other app-level singletons so it's created once at startup, not per-request.
Now let's add a test that hits /search more than the configured limit and asserts we get a 429, to lock in the behavior.
Nice. The test failed though — turns out request.client_id doesn't exist yet, we only have request.remote_addr. Fix it.
Right, routes.py assumed a client_id attribute that middleware.py never set. Simplest fix: use remote_addr as the rate-limit key instead of a nonexistent client_id field.
middleware.py's allow() signature already takes client_id generically so no change needed there — just re-running the test to confirm.
